description: Mercimek Corbasi is a beloved Turkish red lentil soup, known for its vibrant color and incredibly comforting flavor. This hearty and wholesome soup is a staple in Turkish homes, often enjoyed as a starter or a light meal. Its smooth texture and aromatic spices make it a truly satisfying experience for any palate.

instructions.title: Prepare Ingredients
instructions.text: Rinse the red lentils thoroughly under cold running water until the water runs clear. Finely chop the onion and carrot. Mince the garlic cloves. Having everything prepped makes the cooking process smooth.

instructions.title: Sauté Aromatics
instructions.text: In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and carrot and sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent. Stir occasionally to prevent burning.

instructions.title: Add Flavor Base
instructions.text: Add the minced garlic and tomato paste to the pot. Cook for another 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until the tomato paste darkens slightly and becomes fragrant. This step deepens the flavor of the soup.

instructions.title: Combine and Simmer
instructions.text: Stir in the rinsed red lentils, dried mint, and 1/2 teaspoon red pepper flakes. Pour in the vegetable or chicken broth (or water), salt, and black pepper. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils are very tender.

instructions.title: Blend the Soup
instructions.text: Remove the pot from the heat. Using an immersion blender, carefully blend the soup directly in the pot until it is completely smooth. If you don't have an immersion blender, transfer the soup in batches to a regular blender and blend until smooth, then return to the pot. Be careful when blending hot liquids.

instructions.title: Prepare the Topping
instructions.text: In a small saucepan, melt the butter over medium-low heat. Once the butter is melted and slightly foaming, add the remaining 1/2 teaspoon red pepper flakes (pul biber) and stir for about 30 seconds until fragrant. Be careful not to burn the butter or spices.

instructions.title: Serve Mercimek Corbasi
instructions.text: Ladle the hot Mercimek Corbasi into bowls. Drizzle a generous spoonful of the spiced butter topping over each serving. Serve immediately with fresh lemon wedges on the side, allowing each person to squeeze fresh lemon juice into their soup to taste. Afiyet olsun!

tips: For the smoothest soup, ensure your lentils are cooked until very tender before blending. A good immersion blender makes this step quick and easy.
The traditional butter and red pepper flake topping, known as 'nane ve pul biberli tereyağı', is crucial for authentic flavor. Don't skip it!
Mercimek Corbasi tastes even better the next day. Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days.
article:
Discover the heartwarming embrace of Mercimek Corbasi, a staple in Turkish households and a beloved dish worldwide. This vibrant, creamy, and incredibly flavorful red lentil soup is more than just a meal; it’s a taste of Turkish hospitality, a symbol of comfort, and a testament to simple ingredients creating profound deliciousness. Whether you're seeking a nutritious start to your day, a light lunch, or a comforting dinner, Mercimek Corbasi offers a delightful culinary journey. Packed with wholesome goodness and bursting with traditional Turkish spices, it’s a soup that warms both body and soul. Join us as we explore the magic behind this iconic Turkish dish, delve into its authentic preparation, and uncover tips to make it truly spectacular in your own kitchen.

## What is Mercimek Corbasi (Turkish Red Lentil Soup)?

Mercimek Corbasi, pronounced mer-jee-MEK chor-BAH-suh, is a traditional Turkish Red Lentil Soup that holds a cherished place in Turkish cuisine. It’s a velvety, often bright orange-red soup made primarily from red lentils, onions, garlic, tomato paste, and a medley of spices, typically finished with a drizzle of chili-infused butter and dried mint. This beloved Turkish Red Lentil Soup is not just a starter; it's a versatile dish enjoyed at any time of day, from a hearty breakfast to a comforting late-night supper. Its smooth texture and rich, savory flavor profile, enhanced by a hint of tang from lemon juice, make it universally appealing. It’s incredibly nourishing, naturally gluten-free (when prepared without wheat-based additives), and often vegetarian, making it a fantastic option for a wide range of dietary preferences. The soup's ability to be both simple and profoundly satisfying is what makes it a cornerstone of Turkish culinary identity.

## Ingredients for Authentic Mercimek Corbasi

To craft an authentic Turkish Red Lentil Soup, the foundation lies in a few key, high-quality ingredients. The beauty of Mercimek Corbasi is its reliance on pantry staples, transformed into something extraordinary.

*   **Red Lentils (Kırmızı Mercimek):** The star of the show. Split red lentils cook quickly and break down easily, giving the soup its characteristic creamy texture. Ensure they are rinsed thoroughly before use.
*   **Onion:** Provides a sweet and savory base. Yellow or white onions work best.
*   **Garlic:** Adds a pungent depth of flavor that complements the lentils beautifully.
*   **Tomato Paste (Salça):** Essential for adding richness, color, and a subtle tang. Turkish tomato paste is often more concentrated and flavorful.
*   **Spices:**
    *   **Dried Mint (Kuru Nane):** Crucial for the authentic Turkish flavor, especially in the finishing butter drizzle.
    *   **Red Pepper Flakes (Pul Biber or Maras Biber):** Adds a mild warmth and a beautiful red hue to the finishing oil. Adjust to your spice preference.
    *   **Paprika (Tatlı Toz Biber):** For color and a sweet, smoky undertone.
    *   **Cumin (Kimyon):** A classic Turkish spice that adds earthy warmth.
    *   **Salt & Black Pepper:** To taste, for seasoning.
*   **Broth or Water:** Vegetable broth for a vegetarian version, or chicken broth for added depth. Water works perfectly fine too, allowing the lentil flavor to shine.
*   **Butter (Tereyağı) or Olive Oil:** Butter is traditionally used for sautéing and for the finishing drizzle, providing a rich flavor. Olive oil can be used for a lighter or vegan version.
*   **Lemon:** Fresh lemon wedges are served alongside, and a squeeze of juice brightens the soup immensely.

## Step-by-Step Mercimek Corbasi Recipe

Creating this comforting Turkish Red Lentil Soup is surprisingly simple. Follow these steps for a delicious and authentic bowl:

1.  **Prepare the Lentils:** Rinse 1 cup (about 200g) of red lentils under cold running water until the water runs clear. This removes any dust or debris and prevents foaming during cooking. Set aside.

2.  **Sauté Aromatics:** In a large pot or Dutch oven, melt 2 tablespoons of butter (or olive oil) over medium heat. Add 1 finely chopped medium onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add 2 cloves of minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant, being careful not to burn it.

3.  **Build the Flavor Base:** Stir in 1 tablespoon of tomato paste, 1 teaspoon of sweet paprika, and ½ teaspoon of cumin. Cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly, to deepen the flavors of the tomato paste and spices.

4.  **Add Lentils and Liquid:** Add the rinsed red lentils to the pot and stir to coat them with the aromatic mixture. Pour in 6 cups (about 1.5 liters) of hot vegetable or chicken broth (or water). Bring the mixture to a boil.

5.  **Simmer:** Once boiling, reduce the heat to low, cover the pot partially, and let the soup simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils are very tender and have broken down. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.

6.  **Season and Blend:** Season the soup with 1 teaspoon of salt and ½ teaspoon of black pepper, or to taste. For a smooth, creamy texture, use an immersion blender to blend the soup directly in the pot until silky smooth. Alternatively, carefully transfer batches to a regular blender (vent the lid to release steam) and blend until smooth, then return to the pot. If the soup is too thick, add a little more hot broth or water until it reaches your desired consistency.

7.  **Prepare the Chili-Mint Butter (Nane Yağı):** While the soup is simmering or blending, prepare the finishing drizzle. In a small pan, melt 2 tablespoons of butter over medium-low heat. Once melted, remove from heat and stir in 1 teaspoon of dried mint and 1 teaspoon of red pepper flakes (pul biber). The residual heat will toast the spices without burning them, releasing their aroma.

8.  **Serve:** Ladle the hot Mercimek Corbasi into bowls. Drizzle a generous spoonful of the chili-mint butter over each serving. Serve immediately with fresh lemon wedges on the side.

## Tips for the Best Turkish Red Lentil Soup

Achieving that perfect, comforting bowl of Turkish Red Lentil Soup is all about attention to detail.

*   **Rinse Your Lentils Thoroughly:** This is crucial to remove starches and impurities, which can lead to a cloudy soup and affect digestion.
*   **Toast the Tomato Paste and Spices:** Cooking the tomato paste for a minute or two before adding liquid deepens its flavor and color. Similarly, briefly toasting the dry spices releases their aromatic oils, intensifying their taste.
*   **Quality Ingredients Matter:** While simple, the quality of your tomato paste, butter, and especially the dried mint can significantly impact the final flavor. Seek out good Turkish brands if possible.
*   **Don't Skip the Blending:** For the characteristic creamy texture of Mercimek Corbasi, blending is key. An immersion blender makes this step effortless. If you prefer a slightly chunkier texture, blend only half the soup.
*   **Adjust Consistency:** Red lentils absorb a lot of liquid. If your soup is too thick after blending, thin it out with a little extra hot broth or water until it reaches your preferred consistency.
*   **The Finishing Drizzle is Non-Negotiable:** The chili-mint butter (nane yağı) isn't just a garnish; it's an integral part of the Mercimek Corbasi experience. It adds a burst of flavor, aroma, and a beautiful visual contrast. Don't overheat the butter when adding the mint and chili flakes; you want to infuse, not burn.
*   **Fresh Lemon is Key:** A squeeze of fresh lemon juice just before eating brightens the soup's flavors and adds a delightful tangy counterpoint to the richness.

## Serving Suggestions for Mercimek Corbasi

Mercimek Corbasi is a versatile dish that can be enjoyed in many ways. Here are some traditional and popular serving suggestions:

*   **With Lemon Wedges:** This is paramount. Always serve with fresh lemon wedges, allowing each diner to add a squeeze of brightness to their bowl.
*   **Crusty Bread (Ekmek):** A slice of warm, crusty Turkish bread (or any good rustic bread) is perfect for dipping into the rich soup.
*   **Pickles (Turşu):** A side of Turkish pickles offers a delightful tangy crunch that contrasts beautifully with the creamy soup.
*   **Chili Flakes (Pul Biber):** For those who like extra heat, a small bowl of extra red pepper flakes can be offered at the table.
*   **Yogurt (Yoğurt):** While not always traditional, a dollop of plain yogurt or a swirl of sour cream can add a cooling creaminess, especially if you're experimenting with spicier variations.
*   **As a Starter:** Mercimek Corbasi makes an excellent appetizer for a larger Turkish meal, preceding dishes like kebabs or various mezes.
*   **As a Light Meal:** Served with bread and a simple salad, it makes a satisfying and wholesome lunch or dinner.

## Variations & Substitutions

While the classic Turkish Red Lentil Soup recipe is perfect, there are many ways to adapt it to your taste or dietary needs.

*   **Vegetarian/Vegan:** The recipe is easily made vegan by substituting butter with olive oil and using vegetable broth or water.
*   **Adding Vegetables:** For extra nutrition and texture, you can add finely diced carrots or potatoes along with the lentils. They will cook down and thicken the soup further. Some recipes even include a small amount of finely chopped bell pepper for a subtle sweetness.
*   **Spice Variations:** Feel free to adjust the amount of red pepper flakes for more or less heat. A pinch of dried oregano or thyme can also be added for a different aromatic profile, though mint is typically the dominant herb.
*   **Smoked Paprika:** If you enjoy a smoky flavor, use smoked paprika instead of or in addition to sweet paprika.
*   **Lemon Zest:** For an even more intense lemon flavor, add a little lemon zest along with the juice at the end.
*   **Different Lentils:** While red lentils are traditional and ideal for their quick cooking and creamy texture, you could experiment with yellow split peas for a similar result, though the color and flavor profile would subtly change. Green or brown lentils would require longer cooking times and might result in a less smooth soup.
*   **Creaminess without Blending:** If you don't have a blender, you can mash the cooked lentils against the side of the pot with a wooden spoon or potato masher for a slightly chunkier, but still creamy, texture.

Mercimek Corbasi is more than just a soup; it's a culinary journey to the heart of Turkish comfort food. Its simplicity, combined with its rich flavors and nourishing qualities, makes it a timeless classic that appeals to everyone. We encourage you to try making this wonderful Turkish Red Lentil Soup at home, savoring each spoonful of its velvety goodness. It’s a dish that truly embodies warmth, tradition, and the simple joy of good food. Enjoy!
